papers.title: Odour cueing during sleep augments trauma-focused psychotherapy
papers.summary: Combined mechanistic study in healthy participants and randomized clinical trial to test whether odour cueing during sleep augments trauma-focused psychotherapy. In healthy participants, odour re-exposure during sleep increased slow-wave activity and slow oscillations, and greater increases in slow oscillation-spindle coupling were associated with reduced emotional arousal during recall; in PTSD patients, repeated odour cueing over 12 weeks improved clinician-rated and self-reported PTSD symptoms, particularly re-experiencing and negative cognition/mood, and accelerated treatment response and remission.

papers.title: Transcranial photobiomodulation to enhance sleep by elevating adenosine signaling: a translational study.
papers.summary: In mice, transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM) increased NREM sleep and frontal cortex adenosine, while in vitro near-infrared light boosted cellular ATP without cytotoxicity. A double-blind randomized controlled trial with 40 subjects found that tPBM significantly reduced insomnia severity, sleep disturbances, and sleep latency.

papers.title: Short-term environmental enrichment modulates brain region-specific redox responses in adolescent female mice.
papers.summary: Investigated the effects of a three-week environmental enrichment protocol on oxidative balance in hippocampus, hypothalamus, and brainstem of adolescent female C57BL/6 mice. Enrichment reduced protein oxidative damage across all regions but through region-specific patterns: hippocampal dissociated redox profile with increased TBARS and reduced protein carbonylation, hypothalamic non-enzymatic thiol-based buffering, and brainstem SOD-centered defense.

papers.title: Role of the Amygdala in the Complex Relationship Between Sleep and Anxiety.
papers.summary: Review summarizing the amygdala's roles in emotional processing, fear conditioning, and sleep architecture across NREM and REM phases, and discussing its involvement in the cycle of anxiety disorders and sleep disturbances. It also examines how medications for anxiety and sleep disorders act on the amygdala.

papers.title: Cross-Night Modulation of Change Detection ERPs to Foreign Speech Sound Features During N2 Sleep.
papers.summary: Finnish-speaking adults underwent four nights of N2 sleep exposure to tone deviations in vowel /a/ while EEG was recorded. Change detection ERPs P2 and P450 were observed, with P450 amplitude decreasing from night 1 to night 4, but no perceptual learning was found in waking ERPs or behavior.

papers.title: Male and Female Mice Show Similar Fear Memory Performance Despite Hippocampal Immediate Early Gene Expression Differences During Encoding and Consolidation.
papers.summary: Pilot study comparing male and female mice on contextual fear memory (CFM) encoding, consolidation, and recall, and hippocampal immediate early gene expression. Males and females showed no differences in sleep behavior or CFM recall, but females showed a trend for larger CA1 cFos increases during encoding, while only males showed an apparent cFos increase in dentate gyrus during consolidation.

papers.title: Towards continuous brain monitoring: a pilot qualitative study of user experiences with in-ear EEG.
papers.summary: This pilot qualitative study interviewed ten participants after using an in-ear EEG device and identified five themes around acceptability, usability, and conditional adoption, finding that in-ear EEG was perceived as comfortable and comparable to consumer earbuds but adoption depended on demonstrated clinical accuracy.

papers.title: Age and Sex as Moderators of Sleep Architecture in Schizophrenia, Bipolar Disorder, and Unipolar Depression: A Case-Control Polysomnographic Systematic Review and Meta-Regression.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-regression of case-control polysomnographic studies found that study-level mean age and sex composition significantly moderated specific sleep architecture effect sizes in schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and unipolar depression, but demographic factors explained only a modest proportion of between-study heterogeneity.

papers.title: Circadian Biomarkers Before and After the Transition to Spring Daylight Saving Time.
papers.summary: Healthy individuals were assessed before and after the spring DST transition using light sensors, actigraphy, DLMO, and predicted CBT min. The transition had modest, statistically insignificant effects on weekly averages of time in bed, sleepiness, and light-activity synchrony, but slightly delayed CBT min and slightly advanced DLMO and mid-sleep.

papers.title: Dataset Fragmentation, Cognitive Variability, and Reproducibility Challenges in EEG-Based Brain-Computer Interfaces: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-based systematic review of 129 curated publications on public EEG-based BCI datasets identified fragmentation across structural, semantic, procedural, human/contextual, and computational dimensions, and reported median transparency score of 9/10 with data availability in 61.2% and code availability in 20.9%.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm amplification in diabetic retinopathy: a pilot study.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: In this pilot study, eight adults with type 2 diabetes and diabetic retinopathy completed a 6-week behavioral intervention (Amplify-RHYTHM) that significantly reduced insomnia symptoms, sleep midpoint variability, circadian fragmentation, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, while melatonin timing and metabolic parameters remained unchanged.

papers.title: Periodic oscillatory slowing and aperiodic broadband shifts in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder are associated with phenoconversion.
papers.summary: In 134 iRBD patients and 51 controls, periodic and aperiodic EEG components were separated using FOOOF. After aperiodic removal, iRBD showed higher periodic 4-8 Hz power, and converters exhibited more oscillatory slowing and higher occipital aperiodic offset; higher posterior periodic 4-8 Hz power and offset were associated with phenoconversion risk.

papers.title: Early postoperative ward-level circadian-disruptive exposures and short- and long-term outcomes after gastrointestinal cancer surgery: a prospective cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 1500 gastrointestinal cancer surgery patients, higher Ward Circadian Exposure Index (WCEI) during postoperative days 0–3 was associated with increased major complications (adjusted OR 1.38 per SD) and worse disease-free survival (HR 1.29) and overall survival (HR 1.24) at 60 months. However, the association with complications attenuated in a landmark analysis excluding early events, suggesting possible confounding by early clinical deterioration.

papers.title: The Caffeinated Brain Part 3: The Effect of Caffeine on Electroencephalography (EEG) During Wakefulness-A Systematic and Mechanistic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 48 studies found that acute caffeine administration most frequently reduces alpha power and attenuates slow-frequency (theta/delta) activity during states of elevated sleep pressure or withdrawal, but no single reproducible EEG signature or validated biomarker of caffeine response was established due to substantial heterogeneity.

papers.title: Optimized Efficient Channel Attention-based ShuffleNet Framework for EEG Graph-Based Brain Topology Modeling in Motor Imagery Tasks.
papers.summary: An Optimized Deep Learning-based Brain Topology in Motor Imagery Tasks (ODL-BTMIT) framework was proposed, using EEG graph modeling, topological features, and an Efficient Channel Attention-based ShuffleNet optimized with Self-Improved Red Panda Optimization. It achieved 96.5% accuracy with 90% training data and outperformed existing methods with mean accuracy 0.936.

papers.title: Spectral and Directed Connectivity EEG Markers for Classifying Alzheimer's Disease, Frontotemporal Dementia, and Healthy Controls with Exploratory Photobiomodulation Case-Study Projection.
papers.summary: In resting-state EEG from 88 participants (36 AD, 23 FTD, 29 healthy controls), spectral features (especially theta/alpha ratio) and Granger-causality directed connectivity features classified dementia versus healthy controls with balanced accuracy up to 0.710, but AD versus FTD differentiation remained difficult (balanced accuracy 0.584). An exploratory photobiomodulation case study showed longitudinal EEG changes including increased alpha power and HC-like connectivity projections.

papers.title: Montage-guided fusion network for long-term scalp electroencephalography seizure detection.
papers.summary: Proposes MGF-Net, a montage-guided fusion network that models 18 bipolar EEG derivations as nodes in a relation-labeled graph with a graph Transformer for seizure detection. On the CHB-MIT dataset, it achieved event-level sensitivity of 100% with a false detection rate of 0.82/h and latency of 2.03 s.

papers.title: Cell-Autonomous and Systemic Circadian Regulation of Gene Expression in Adipocytes.
papers.summary: Deeply sequenced in vitro-differentiated adipocytes over a 2.5-day circadian time-course and compared with in vivo adipose tissue datasets, finding 21% of the protein-coding transcriptome rhythmic. Motif enrichment revealed temporally distinct early E-box activator and late nuclear receptor-associated regulatory programs in adipocytes.

papers.title: Timing of Parenteral Nutrition in Neonates, Infants, and Children: Current Evidence, Circadian Considerations, and Emerging Directions.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the timing, duration, and 24-hour delivery pattern of parenteral nutrition (PN) in neonates, infants, and children, including circadian considerations. It reports that early PN remains standard for very preterm/very low birth weight infants while delayed PN is associated with improved outcomes in critically ill children, and that continuous versus cyclic PN use differs by age and stability, with clinical implications of circadian-aligned overnight infusion largely unestablished.

papers.title: The Oral-Brain Axis: A Unified Framework Linking Trigeminal Sensorimotor Dysfunction, Chronic Stress, Neuroinflammation, and Neurodegeneration.
papers.summary: This review proposes an oral-brain axis model in which chronic trigeminal sensorimotor dysfunction (e.g., occlusal mismatch, impaired mastication, sleep bruxism, sleep-disordered breathing) generates persistent prediction errors in the mesencephalic trigeminal nucleus (MesV), recruiting the locus coeruleus and its asparagine endopeptidase (LC-AEP) pathway to drive neuroimmune activation, tau pathology, and neurodegeneration. It cites epidemiological associations of tooth loss and impaired mastication with dementia risk and prodromal Parkinson's models showing early trigeminal sensory-processing abnormalities before motor symptoms.

papers.title: Efficacy of Physical Exercise in Ameliorating Circadian Rhythm Disruption-Related Intestinal Inflammation: A Benefit Correlated with Reduced Chenodeoxycholic Acid.
papers.summary: Combining Mendelian randomization, a circadian rhythm disruption mouse model, and multi-omics, this study found that physical exercise ameliorated CRD-related intestinal inflammation in mice, and this benefit was associated with reduced chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA) and enhanced intestinal clock gene expression and Prevotella. Oral CDCA administration dampened the anti-inflammatory effect of exercise.

papers.title: Dietary Carotenoid Intake and Sleep: A Narrative Review of Evidence from Human and In Vivo Animal Studies.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized 29 human observational/intervention and in vivo animal studies on dietary carotenoids and sleep. Observational studies generally linked higher carotenoid intake or serum concentrations to better sleep outcomes, 9 of 11 intervention studies (81.8%) reported improvement in at least one sleep-related outcome though not always significant versus placebo, and preclinical work showed dose-dependent increases in total and non-REM sleep and reduced wakefulness.

papers.title: Factors associated with sleep state misperception in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 700 OSA patients classified into negative, normal, and positive sleep state misperception groups based on Sleep Perception Index. Higher AHI was independently associated with both misperception directions, with positive misperception linked to objective sleep architecture disruptions and negative misperception to psychological and cognitive factors.

papers.title: Intermittent Hypoxia-Induced Inflammation and the Formation of Exhaled Volatile Organic Compound Profiles in Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how intermittent hypoxia-induced inflammation in obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) may shape exhaled volatile organic compound (VOC) profiles, focusing on pathways such as NF-κB, HIF-1α, and NLRP3 that could alter aldehydes, alkanes, acetone, alcohols, and isoprene via oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and metabolic reprogramming. It reports that clinical studies suggest exhaled VOCs may associate with disease severity, nocturnal hypoxic burden, metabolic abnormalities, and treatment response, but specificity and reproducibility remain limited by individual and methodological heterogeneity.

papers.title: Critical Care Monitoring in Comatose Patients Receiving ECMO: A Cohort Study of Machine Learning on Quantitative EEG for Diagnosing Acute Brain Injury and Prognosticating Mortality.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study applied machine learning to quantitative EEG features in 57 comatose ECMO patients to diagnose acute brain injury (ABI) and predict 30-day mortality. Models incorporating qEEG achieved an AUC of 0.769 for ABI detection and 0.864 for mortality prediction, with frontal theta power and interhemispheric asymmetry as key features.

papers.title: Association between female hormone intake and circadian syndrome: A cross-sectional study based on NHANES 2005-2018.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional NHANES 2005-2018 study of 7,279 nonpregnant women aged ≥20 examined the association between female hormone intake and circadian syndrome (CircS), which had a weighted prevalence of 54.4%. Female hormone intake was independently associated with increased CircS odds (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.20-1.80, P<.001), and restricted cubic spline analysis found nonlinear age and BMI associations with inflection points at 61.0 years and 29.9 kg/m2.

papers.title: Systemic inflammatory profiles associated with early EEG abnormalities following ischemic stroke: a cohort study.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort of 307 acute ischemic stroke patients examined associations between peripheral inflammatory biomarkers and early EEG abnormalities within 72 h. Elevated neutrophil count was independently associated with epileptiform discharges (OR 1.19) and improved prediction, while slow activity was mainly predicted by stroke severity and hemorrhagic transformation.

papers.title: Sleep-Autonomic Interactions in Parkinson's Disease and Multiple System Atrophy: A Comparative Study Using Structural Equation Modeling.
papers.summary: This study used structural equation modeling to compare sleep and autonomic profiles in 136 drug-naïve Parkinson's disease (PD) and 67 multiple system atrophy (MSA) patients, finding greater sleep and autonomic impairment in MSA. In MSA, autonomic dysfunction was significantly associated with increased sleep disruption (β = -0.68, P = 0.006) with higher explanatory power (R² = 0.54) than in PD (R² = 0.29).

papers.title: Sleep, Stress, Circadian Rhythm, and Diet in Pediatric Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the impact of sleep, psychological stress, circadian rhythm, and diet on pediatric disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBIs), highlighting their bidirectional interactions through neuroendocrine, autonomic, immune, and microbial pathways. It emphasizes the need for a biopsychosocial approach and further prospective pediatric studies to clarify causality.

papers.title: Ayurveda Treatments for Insomnia: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review evaluated clinical and mechanistic evidence for Ayurvedic treatments for insomnia, finding that standardized Withania somnifera extract has the most rigorous support for reducing sleep-onset latency and improving sleep efficiency, while external therapies like Shirodhara show favorable autonomic changes but weak evidence. Overall certainty remains low due to risk of bias and lack of long-term safety data.

papers.title: Disease Course Map progression markers transfer from isolated REM sleep behavior disorder to non-RBD prodromal alpha-synucleinopathy: a PPMI study of 1,499 participants.
papers.summary: Applied Disease Course Map (DCM) progression markers from iRBD to 1,499 non-RBD prodromal participants in PPMI, showing high ranking concordance (ρ = 0.87–0.97) without recalibration. Earlier onset and faster progression were associated with lower striatal dopamine transporter binding and α-synuclein SAA positivity, supporting DCM markers as continuous endpoints in non-RBD prodromal synucleinopathy.

papers.title: Drug-Induced Sleep Endoscopy in Pediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Clinical Applications, Classification Systems, and Anesthetic Considerations.
papers.summary: This review evaluates drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) in pediatric obstructive sleep apnea, assessing airway assessment, classification systems, anesthesia protocols, and surgical decision-making. It reports that DISE altered surgical plans in 30–60% of patients and that dexmedetomidine best approximates NREM sleep, while the lack of a universally accepted pediatric-specific classification system limits comparability and evidence-based algorithms.

papers.title: Accelerated Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation for the Treatment of Alcohol Use Disorder: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Study With Six-Month Follow-Up.
papers.summary: This randomized sham-controlled trial tested accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (a-iTBS) vs traditional iTBS vs sham in 61 male inpatients with alcohol use disorder. Although the primary craving outcome did not differ significantly among groups, a-iTBS showed a higher response rate, earlier response onset, and longer abstinence duration at 6-month follow-up than sham.

papers.title: Hybrid Digital Twin Framework for Personalized Diabetes Management Using Mathematical Modelling and Machine Learning.
papers.summary: This study proposes a digital twin-based insulin dosage simulator for personalized diabetes management, integrating machine learning, the Bergman Minimal Model, a circadian insulin sensitivity model, Bayesian risk estimation, and explainable AI. Simulation results showed improved glucose prediction accuracy, enhanced hypoglycemia risk detection, and optimized insulin dosing strategies compared with traditional approaches.

papers.title: International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology standardized stereo-electroencephalography terminology.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This IFCN guideline developed standardized stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) terminology through a modified Delphi process with 41 experts. The resulting glossary defines key background activities, interictal and ictal patterns, electrical stimulation responses, and common artifacts, providing a framework to improve consistency and multicenter collaboration in presurgical epilepsy evaluation.

papers.title: Managing Type 1 Diabetes in Neurodiverse Children and Young People: A Qualitative Exploration of Complexity and Care Challenges.
papers.summary: This qualitative study used semi-structured interviews with 15 neurodiverse children and young people (age 12-18) with Type 1 diabetes and 13 parent caregivers to explore barriers and challenges in diabetes management. Key themes included caregiver adaptation of routines, central role of family support, sleep disturbance from fear of hypoglycemia improved by continuous glucose monitoring, and perceived benefits of diabetes technologies despite sensory challenges.

papers.title: Music-based interventions in adult stroke rehabilitation: a narrative review of clinical applications, proposed mechanisms, and implementation.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized clinical applications, proposed mechanisms, and implementation considerations of music-based interventions in adult stroke rehabilitation. The strongest evidence supports rhythmic auditory stimulation for gait and selected music-supported upper-limb programs, while melodic intonation therapy may improve trained utterances in nonfluent aphasia but transfer to everyday communication remains uncertain.

papers.title: Fahr syndrome in an 18-year-old male with pseudohypoparathyroidism: Clinical-radiological dissociation.
papers.summary: This case report describes an 18-year-old male with pseudohypoparathyroidism presenting with headaches, carpopedal spasms, and depressed mood after medication non-compliance, with extensive bilateral intracranial calcifications on imaging despite largely unremarkable neurological examination. Calcium and calcitriol supplementation resolved spasms and improved headaches and mood at 15-day follow-up, illustrating clinical-radiological dissociation in Fahr syndrome.

papers.title: Occupational Stressors, Working Conditions and Self-Reported Mental Health Among Veterinarians in Germany: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Survey.
papers.summary: This exploratory cross-sectional survey of 126 veterinarians in Germany assessed occupational stressors, working conditions, job satisfaction, and self-reported mental health. The greatest perceived stress was related to work-life balance and working hours, and frequently reported symptoms included sleep disturbances (63.5%), burnout symptoms (31.7%), and anxiety (26.2%), with only 19.0% having sought psychological help.

papers.title: Peri-operative management of patients having day surgery: a consensus statement from the Association of Anaesthetists, British Association for Day Surgery and the Association of Paediatric Anaesthetists, Great Britain and Ireland.
papers.summary: This consensus statement from UK anesthesia associations used a targeted literature review and modified Delphi process to develop recommendations for peri-operative management of day surgery in adults and children. Recommendations cover patient selection, pre-assessment, comorbidities, surgical procedures, logistical considerations, anaesthetic techniques, and discharge processes to support healthcare providers in optimizing day surgery services.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
